annotation.title_clean: Model Predictive Degree of Automation Regulation for Mobile Robots Using Robot Vitals and Robot Health
annotation.title_en: Model Predictive Degree of Automation Regulation for Mobile Robots Using Robot Vitals and Robot Health
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Braun, C.A.; Ramesh, A.; Rothfuss, S.; Chiou, M.; Stolkin, R.; Hohmann, S.
annotation.summary_en: Engineering paper proposing a model-predictive controller that automatically regulates a mobile robot's degree and level of automation in human-robot teams, using 'robot vitals' and 'robot health' as performance-degradation metrics. Preliminary feasibility studies are reported. It contains no governance or legal content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Model predictive architecture for degree-of-automation (DOA) and level-of-automation (LOA) regulation
Robot health, computed from robot vitals, is the optimisation objective
With linear blending, the optimum lies at the boundaries of alpha, so traded control is optimal
Preliminary simulation studies with sensor noise and operator distraction show feasibility
